chunks.arabic_text: أَبِي رَحِمَهُ ٱللَّهُ قَالَ حَدَّثَنَا سَعْدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ عَبْدِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ قَالَ

translations.en: My father, Allah may have mercy upon him, narrated to us from Sa’d ibn Abdullah, from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said:

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ ٱللَّهِ ع يَا عَلِيَّ بْنَ عَبْدِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ لَا يَغُرَّنَّكَ بُكَاؤُهُمْ فَإِنَّ ٱلتَّقْوَىٰ فِي ٱلْقَلْبِ.

translations.en: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: O Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, do not be deceived by their weeping, for God-consciousness is in the heart.

en.summary: In this narration from *Sifat al-Shia*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) cautions Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz against mistaking external emotional displays, like weeping, for genuine spiritual depth, asserting that true piety (*taqwa*) is an internal state of the heart. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *batin* (inner reality) over *zahir* (outer appearance), aligning with the concept of *ikhlas* (sincerity) where the heart's condition determines the validity of worship. The reference to Surah At-Tawbah 9:108 underscores the contrast between outward piety and inner truth, further supported by Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13, which defines true nobility as God-consciousness rooted in the heart.
en.seo_question: What is the difference between outward weeping and true piety in Shia hadith?
